question: Did CvSU or PEMSEA publish a separate, comprehensive final output for the parent Imus River watershed biophysical-characterization and pollution-assessment project beyond the crosswalked ASEANO studies?

sources: Official CvSU Research Center project listing
CvSU January 2021 Research and Extension newsletter
CvSU September 2022 Research and Extension newsletter
PEMSEA ASEANO project page and report catalog
PEMSEA page and PDF for the CvSU watershed-mapping component
queryFamilies: Exact parent title and spelling variants on cvsu.edu.ph
Imus River Watershed plus final report or PDF on cvsu.edu.ph
Parent title plus CvSU on pemsea.org and SEA Knowledge Bank
Biophysical Characterization plus Imus River on the DLSU-D research portal
searchScope.boundary: Public indexed and directly opened institutional pages/documents only. This is not an exhaustive search of private, restricted, unindexed, or offline CvSU archives.

sourceReviews.finding: CvSU's Research Center project listing names the parent Imus River Watershed project, Prof. Noel A. Sedigo, PEMSEA funding, and a November 2020-April 2021 duration. The page does not link a comprehensive final report or provide fish methods, taxa, or a dataset. Its current section is headed On-going Projects despite the dated project period, so it is treated as a project-catalog entry, not a current status update.

CvSU's January 2021 newsletter describes the parent project as planned work and lists five ASEANO studies, including CvSU Studies 4 and 5. It gives a January-June 2021 period, different from the Research Center listing.

The September 2022 CvSU newsletter describes a symposium for completed R&D projects held on September 8 and lists the Imus watershed parent project among the Natural and Life Science awardees. It names the project team but supplies no standalone project report, fish-data table, methods, station list, or dataset link. The recognition supports completed-project context, not access to or completeness of a final technical deliverable.

PEMSEA's public ASEANO catalog lists the Imus baseline, the five crosswalked study reports, and other toolkit/proceedings outputs. No separate comprehensive report under CvSU's full parent-project title is exposed in the reviewed catalog.

The public Study 4 watershed-mapping report is one confirmed CvSU component output. Its title, mapping scope, and authorship do not establish that it is the comprehensive parent-project deliverable. The five-study crosswalk remains the controlling component-level reconciliation.

reconciliation.publiclyCatalogedProjectOutputs: CvSU's January 2021 newsletter names five planned studies; the existing crosswalk links all five to public ASEANO report candidates. PEMSEA's broader project page also lists baseline and knowledge products beyond those five.
reconciliation.parentProjectOutput: No standalone comprehensive final technical report under the full CvSU parent-project title was located in the bounded institutional-source search. The completed-project symposium record does not supply or identify such a file.
reconciliation.interpretation: The search result is an access and catalog gap only. A final report, annexes, data, or additional outputs may exist in CvSU or partner archives and were not ruled out.

fishEvidenceReview.interpretation: The parent-project listing, newsletters, report catalog, and component crosswalk do not disclose site/date/method/taxon-level fish data. No fish presence or absence conclusion is supported.

rightsReview.decision: Retain bibliographic metadata and short factual research notes only. Do not reproduce report text, maps, tables, or datasets without item-specific reuse review.

limitations: A bounded indexed search cannot establish that an output is unpublished or unavailable from an institutional library, author, or restricted repository.
CvSU's 2022 symposium recognition is completion context, not the final technical report itself.
The January 2021 planned period and Research Center listed duration differ and remain unresolved.
No reviewed public summary provides fish collection methods, dates, stations, taxa, vouchers, or a reusable dataset.
No current water-quality safety, fishing legality, species absence, diet, or geometry claim follows from this review.
nextAction: Continue independent public fish-source discovery. If the parent project becomes a priority, use CvSU's authorized Research Information System or Research Center access route to request the consolidated final report, appendices, fish-sampling methods and site/date/taxon table if any, voucher or identification support, and item-specific reuse terms. Keep any inquiry unsent unless separately authorized.
